chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله taught ʿAlī, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, a thousand letters; each letter opens a thousand letters.

key_terms.أَلْفَ: a thousand; indicating vastness and abundance
key_terms.حَرْفٍ: letter; a unit of transmitted knowledge in this report
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.عَلِيًّا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the direct recipient of this teaching
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ: opens; unfolds or leads to further knowledge

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī narrate about the knowledge taught by Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conveyed immense knowledge to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام. It highlights the uniquely expansive and unfolding nature of the knowledge entrusted to him, indicating his distinguished rank in receiving prophetic teaching.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Bakr Al Hazaramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> taught Ali<sup>asws</sup> a thousand letters, each letter opening a thousand letters’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Bakr al-Hadrami from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following. “
the Messenger of Allah made Ali (a.s.) learn a thousand letters of which each one opens a thousand letters.”
